summary: Generates SMPTE linear timecode as an audio signal for routing to audio output or other LTC-aware systems.
key_concepts: Outputs SMPTE linear timecode encoded as an audio signal that can be routed to Audio Device Out CHOP.
Play Mode can run sequentially or reference timecode from a CHOP, DAT, or Timecode Class object.
Play, Cue, Cue Pulse, and initial frame/second/minute/hour parameters define whether the output advances or holds a starting time.
Frame Rate usually sits between 24 and 30; rates above 30 use non-standard user-bit behavior and may not be readable by other systems.
Drop Frame Numbering implements 29.97 NTSC-style skipped frame numbers, while High FPS Behaviour cycles or duplicates LTC frame counts.
User Data fields 1-8 write custom user bits, commonly used for reel number or date metadata.

key_params.name: playmode
key_params.note: Sequential or reference a Timecode object/CHOP/DAT

key_params.name: cue
key_params.note: Hold output at initial values while on

key_params.name: cuepulse
key_params.note: Pulse to reset output to initial values

key_params.name: highfpsbehaviour
key_params.note: Frame counting behavior above LTC frame rate

common_gotchas: LTC Out produces an audio signal; route it to Audio Device Out CHOP or another audio path for physical output.
Use Info CHOP to inspect the timecode currently being output.
Standard LTC is limited to 30 fps; higher frame rates use custom user-bit behavior and may not be readable by other software/devices.
Drop-frame numbering skips frame numbers 0 and 1 at the first second of most minutes for 29.97 NTSC compatibility.
Cue holds initial values while enabled; Cue Pulse resets once and then play behavior resumes.
